title: Severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis)
dispatcher_summary: Suspected anaphylaxis; epinephrine auto-injector use being assisted if available.
clarifying_question: Do they have swelling of the face or throat, hives, or trouble breathing after contact with an allergen?

steps.text: If the person has an epinephrine auto-injector, help them use it on the outer thigh right away.
steps.spoken: If they have an epinephrine pen, use it now on the outer thigh.

steps.text: Lay them flat with legs raised. If breathing is difficult, let them sit up. If vomiting, lay on side.
steps.spoken: Lay them flat with legs raised. If they struggle to breathe, let them sit up.

steps.text: If symptoms do not improve in 5-15 minutes and a second injector is available, give it.
steps.spoken: If no better in five to fifteen minutes and you have a second pen, use it.

steps.text: If they stop breathing, start CPR.
steps.spoken: If they stop breathing, start CPR.

source: Red Cross / FARE anaphylaxis guidance (to be verified by reviewer)
